amour-2012.gazette: Haneke shot Amour almost entirely inside one Paris apartment, holding the camera still and letting the frame do the work — no score beyond what the characters play, no cutaway to soften a stroke or a bad night. Jean-Louis Trintignant and Emmanuelle Riva were both in their eighties when they made it. The film took the Palme d'Or in 2012, and Riva became the oldest Best Actress nominee in Academy history.

argo-2012.gazette: The 1980 rescue of six American diplomats from Tehran was known for years as the Canadian Caper: Ambassador Ken Taylor and his staff hid them, and Ottawa issued the passports that carried them out. Argo puts a CIA officer at the center and adds a runway chase that never happened. Taylor pressed Affleck on the balance, and the closing text was rewritten before release.

barbara-2012.gazette: Petzold set Barbara in a provincial hospital on the Baltic coast in the summer of 1980 and refused the usual shorthand for East Germany — no Trabant gags, no kitsch shop window. The period arrives as procedure instead: exit-visa paperwork, unannounced apartment searches, the strip search a doctor under suspicion is expected to submit to. Authenticity here is a claim that can be checked surface by surface.
barbara-2012.prism: Stripping out the kitsch also strips out the comfort — without Trabant jokes to laugh at, the surveillance has nowhere to go but into ordinary rooms. The cost of getting it right is that nothing in the frame lets you off.

lincoln-2012.gazette: Lincoln builds its last act on the January 1865 House vote on the Thirteenth Amendment, drawing on Doris Kearns Goodwin's account and the congressional record of the roll call. The roll call is also where the film departs from it: two Connecticut members are shown voting nay, though the state's delegation voted yes to a man. A sitting Connecticut congressman wrote to Spielberg about it after release.

searching-for-sugar-man-2012.gazette: The film follows two South Africans tracking down Sixto Rodriguez, a Detroit musician whose early-seventies albums failed at home and sold heavily under apartheid. What it leaves out is that Rodriguez had already been found once: he toured Australia in the late seventies and again in the early eighties, with a live album released there. The omission surfaced almost as soon as the film won its Academy Award.

stories-we-tell-2012.gazette: Polley built the film out of primary material — interviews with her siblings and her father, her mother's letters, audio recorded across the whole inquiry. The home movies threaded through it are not all home movies: much of the Super 8 was staged and shot for the film, with actors. Polley discloses this near the end, after an hour in which the footage has been read as evidence.
stories-we-tell-2012.prism: Once you know the grain was manufactured, every earlier certainty has to be re-filed. That is the point and also the price — the film demonstrates how easily testimony gets built by using you as the demonstration.

the-hunt-2012.gazette: Vinterberg came out of Dogme 95, the 1995 vow that banned score, artificial light, and any prop brought to location. The Hunt keeps the method without the manifesto: handheld camera, available light in a Danish provincial town, a rumour moving between a kindergarten and a hunting club. Mads Mikkelsen took the Cannes acting prize for it in 2012.

zero-dark-thirty-2012.gazette: Bigelow and Boal reconstructed the decade-long CIA hunt that ended in Abbottabad in May 2011, working from reporting and access the agency itself later had to account for. Within weeks of release, senior members of the Senate Intelligence Committee wrote to the studio disputing the film's suggestion that torture produced the courier's name. The committee's own study of the detention program reached the opposite conclusion.

12-years-a-slave-2013.gazette: Northup published Twelve Years a Slave in 1853, months after his release, and named the men who kidnapped and held him. Historians have since matched much of it against court filings, bills of sale, and parish records, and an annotated edition traced the plantations by name. McQueen shot in Louisiana, on ground within reach of the places the book describes.
12-years-a-slave-2013.prism: Verifiability was the memoir's weapon — a free man's papers were the only thing that ever got him out, and the same paper trail is what lets historians confirm him now. The record survives because slavery was an economy, and economies keep books.

a-touch-of-sin-2013.gazette: Jia drew each of the four episodes from incidents that had already circulated on Chinese social media: a Shanxi villager who shot the officials running his privatized mine, a woman who stabbed an official at a sauna, a young worker who went off a factory dormitory. He kept the geography and the sequence of events largely intact. The film won best screenplay at Cannes in 2013 and was never released in mainland China.

blue-is-the-warmest-color-2013.gazette: Kechiche shot for months and exposed hundreds of hours of film, running takes long past the point where most productions stop. The realism was the working method itself: rehearse it, wear it down, keep rolling until the performance stops reading as one. The 2013 Palme d'Or went jointly to the director and both lead actresses, which the festival had not done before.

child-s-pose-2013.gazette: Netzer's camera stays handheld and close through Bucharest apartments, a police station, and a morgue corridor, in the flat available light the Romanian New Wave has worked in since the mid-2000s. The plot runs as procedure: a wealthy mother works her contacts after her son kills a child on the road. It took the Golden Bear at Berlin in 2013.
child-s-pose-2013.prism: The style is what makes the class argument land — shot like documentary, the bribes look like errands, which is exactly how they function. Nothing in the film has to accuse anyone; the room does it.

dallas-buyers-club-2013.gazette: Woodroof was a Dallas electrician who tested positive in the mid-eighties, began importing unapproved drugs from Mexico, and ran a subscription buyers club until his death in 1992. The two people closest to him on screen were invented — Rayon and the doctor are composites written for the film. People who knew Woodroof have also disputed the homophobia the script gives him at the start.

like-father-like-son-2013.gazette: Kore-eda works with child actors by withholding the script and feeding lines on the day, a practice carried over from his years in documentary television. Like Father, Like Son builds on a hospital switch at birth, drawn from real mix-ups in postwar Japan, some of which reached the courts decades later. It took the Jury Prize at Cannes in 2013.

still-life-2013.gazette: UK councils are legally obliged to bury or cremate anyone who dies alone in their district with no one to arrange it; the duty sits in public-health law, and the officers who carry it out are ordinary municipal staff. Pasolini built the film around one such officer in a South London borough, following the paper each case leaves behind — a rent book, a photograph, a name in an address book. It premiered at Venice in 2013.
still-life-2013.prism: The job exists because the state decided an unclaimed body is a public-health matter, not because anyone decided the dead were owed a service. Everything the officer adds — the music, the words, the search for one mourner — is off the books, which is why it is the first thing a budget cut removes.
